_meta.name: Business Operations Atlas (LIMEN repo seed)
_meta.source: Business Operations Atlas + Companion (Business professor and scientist project). Grounded in NAICS 2022, ISIC, SOC 2018, O*NET, GICS, APQC PCF.
_meta.seed_scope: This repo seed contains the UNIVERSAL frameworks (reusable across all 20 domains) plus ONE fully-imported domain: finance (the executed proof for the motif x APQC crosswalk). The remaining 19 domains append in the identical shape and are listed in _domain_manifest as pending import.
_meta.faithful_note: Universal block and finance business types / regulators / positions are reproduced faithfully from source (identifiers: naics, socCode, jurisdiction, examples preserved). Finance view100k long-form essays (role/interdependencies) are summarized here; the crosswalk consumes businessTypes + positions mechanism prose, which is preserved verbatim.

frameworks.name: NAICS 2022
frameworks.purpose: Definitive taxonomy of what businesses DO; every North American establishment classified by primary production process. U.S. Census Bureau.

frameworks.name: ISIC Rev. 4 / Rev. 5
frameworks.purpose: UN worldwide equivalent; root taxonomy for national systems (NACE, ANZSIC).

frameworks.name: SOC 2018
frameworks.purpose: Definitive taxonomy of what WORKERS do. BLS.

frameworks.name: O*NET-SOC
frameworks.purpose: Deepest occupational database: tasks, tools, knowledge, skills, work context, education, wages. U.S. DOL.

frameworks.name: GICS
frameworks.purpose: How the FINANCIAL world classifies companies (MSCI/S&P). Investment/indexing.

frameworks.name: APQC PCF
frameworks.purpose: Standard taxonomy of business OPERATIONS; every internal activity in a numbered hierarchy for benchmarking.

legalForms.name: Sole Proprietorship
legalForms.definition: One person owns and IS the business; no legal separation.
legalForms.share: ~73% of U.S. businesses by count, ~4% of receipts.

legalForms.name: General / Limited Partnership (GP, LP, LLP)
legalForms.definition: Two or more co-owners share profits per agreement; LLPs shield professionals from partners' malpractice.
legalForms.share: Standard for law firms, PE funds, family enterprises.

legalForms.name: Limited Liability Company (LLC)
legalForms.definition: Hybrid: corporate liability protection with partnership tax flexibility.

legalForms.name: C-Corporation
legalForms.definition: Legal person separate from owners; perpetual life, transferable shares; double taxation.
legalForms.share: ~1.7M U.S. C-corps produce the majority of business receipts.

legalForms.name: S-Corporation
legalForms.definition: Corporation electing pass-through taxation; <=100 shareholders, one class of stock.
legalForms.share: ~5M U.S. entities; most common corporate form by count.

legalForms.name: Benefit Corporation / B-Corp
legalForms.definition: For-profit legally bound to consider social/environmental impact.

legalForms.name: Cooperative
legalForms.definition: Owned and democratically controlled by members; one member, one vote.
legalForms.share: ~30,000 U.S. co-ops; dominant in farm marketing and rural utilities.

legalForms.name: Nonprofit / 501(c)(3)
legalForms.definition: Mission-owned; no shareholders; surpluses reinvested in mission.

legalForms.name: Joint Venture / Strategic Alliance
legalForms.definition: Two or more firms co-own an entity or pool capabilities for a defined purpose.
legalForms.share: Standard vehicle for megaprojects and tech-sharing.

legalForms.name: State-Owned / Government Enterprise
legalForms.definition: Commercial enterprise owned wholly or partly by the state.
legalForms.share: Many of the world's largest energy, banking, rail firms.

legalForms.name: Holding Company / Conglomerate
legalForms.definition: Owns controlling stakes in operating subsidiaries rather than operating itself.
legalForms.share: Architecture of nearly every large multi-business enterprise.

legalForms.name: Franchise
legalForms.definition: Brand owner licenses its business system to independent owner-operators.

universalLadder.what: Residual claimants; supply equity, bear ultimate risk, hold the ultimate vote (elect directors, approve mergers, amend charters).
Fiduciary body; duties of care and loyalty; hires/fires CEO, approves strategy, budgets, major transactions, pay. Works through Audit, Compensation, Nominating/Governance, Risk committees.
Single point of accountability for the whole enterprise; sets strategy, allocates capital and talent, owns operating model and culture. SOC 11-1011.
Each owns an enterprise-wide system: CFO, COO, CTO/CIO, CMO, CHRO, GC/CLO, CRO, CCO, CISO, CSO. Legally appointed by the board; can bind the company.

universalLadder.tier: Presidents / EVPs / SVPs of Business Units
universalLadder.what: Own a full P&L (division, region, product line); mini-CEOs translating enterprise strategy into unit plans.
Own a function or portfolio within a unit; convert annual plans into quarterly execution. Where most coordination happens.
Front line of management; own a team of 5-15; hire, train, schedule, review, remove blockers.
Expert individual contributors (engineers, accountants, analysts, attorneys); many individually licensed, importing professional-body regulation into the firm.
Those who physically make, move, serve, fix, protect; majority of civilization's workers; measured on safety, quality, throughput.

coreFunctions.name: Finance & Accounting
coreFunctions.what: Keeps score and allocates fuel: bookkeeping, reporting (GAAP/IFRS), FP&A, treasury, tax, audit, capital procurement. SEC/SOX/PCAOB.

coreFunctions.name: Operations / Production
coreFunctions.what: Converts inputs into product/service: manufacturing, service delivery, quality (ISO 9001, Six Sigma), capacity, maintenance.

coreFunctions.name: Sales & Business Development
coreFunctions.what: Converts demand into revenue: pipeline, quota sellers, account management, pricing execution.

coreFunctions.name: Marketing
coreFunctions.what: Creates and shapes demand: brand, product marketing, demand gen, research, pricing strategy. FTC/BBB.

coreFunctions.name: Human Resources / People
coreFunctions.what: Acquires and develops workforce: recruiting, comp/benefits, learning, performance, labor relations. EEOC/DOL/OSHA/NLRB/ERISA.

coreFunctions.name: Information Technology
coreFunctions.what: Runs the firm's nervous system: infrastructure, applications, data, cybersecurity. ITIL/COBIT/NIST; GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA.

coreFunctions.name: Legal, Risk & Compliance
coreFunctions.what: Keeps the firm inside the lines: contracts, litigation, IP, regulatory filings, ethics, ERM, internal audit.

coreFunctions.name: Research & Development
coreFunctions.what: Builds the future offer: applied research, product development, engineering, design.

coreFunctions.name: Supply Chain & Logistics
coreFunctions.what: Moves atoms: sourcing, purchasing, inventory, warehousing, transportation, S&OP.

coreFunctions.name: Corporate Strategy & Development
coreFunctions.what: Decides where to play and how to win: strategic planning, M&A, partnerships, competitive intelligence, transformation.

regulationLayers.name: Layer 1 - State Regulation (vertical)
regulationLayers.what: Governments license, inspect, sanction. Designated watchdogs per domain; treaty bodies above nations (WTO, BIS/Basel, ICAO/IMO, WHO).

regulationLayers.name: Layer 2 - Self-Regulation (internal)
regulationLayers.what: Industries police themselves: SROs with teeth (FINRA, state bars, medical boards), accreditation, standards bodies (ISO/ANSI/IEEE), codes of ethics.

regulationLayers.name: Layer 3 - Mutual / Market Regulation (horizontal)
regulationLayers.what: Businesses regulate each other: auditors, rating agencies, insurers, exchanges, covenants, supplier codes, reputation systems.

sizeClasses.name: Small business
sizeClasses.note: U.S. small businesses employ ~46% of the private workforce.

domains.name: Finance
domains.tagline: The intermediation of capital across time, space, and risk.

view100k.role_summary: Civilization's capital-allocation and risk-transfer machinery (Merton's six functions: clearing payments, pooling savings, transferring resources across time/space, managing risk, producing price information, mitigating incentive/information problems). Defining peculiarity is leverage: a bank at 10:1 makes system stability a public good, which is why finance is regulated more like a utility than its private profits suggest.
view100k.regulationModel_summary: Densest regulatory lattice of any private industry, layered by function and charter (Fed, OCC, FDIC, SEC, CFTC, CFPB, FinCEN, state insurance/NAIC). Statutory self-regulation via FINRA/NFA/exchanges. International: Basel, IOSCO, FSB, IAIS, FATF. Beneath all: market discipline (rating agencies, short sellers, counterparty limits, funding markets), harnessed via disclosure.

view10k.overview: NAICS Sector 52. Structurally organized by balance-sheet model: spread businesses earning net interest margin on leveraged balance sheets (banks, insurers); fee businesses earning on flows/assets (asset managers, brokers, payment networks); risk-transfer businesses earning underwriting margin (insurance, derivatives dealing).

businessTypes.name: Commercial Bank (Money-Center / Regional / Community)
businessTypes.definition: Chartered depository taking insured deposits and extending commercial, real estate, and consumer credit; operates the core payment accounts of the economy.
businessTypes.operations: Earns net interest margin plus fees; runs credit underwriting committees, asset-liability management (ALCO) of interest-rate risk, branch/digital service, and BSA/AML transaction monitoring.
businessTypes.regulation: OCC/Fed/FDIC + state; FDIC insurance; Basel III capital/liquidity. Self-regulates via ABA codes, three-lines-of-defense internal audit.
businessTypes.examples: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, PNC, a typical $1B community bank

businessTypes.name: Investment Bank / Broker-Dealer
businessTypes.definition: Underwrites debt/equity, advises on M&A, makes markets, executes trades.
businessTypes.operations: Revenue from advisory fees, underwriting spreads, sales-and-trading; deal teams, trading desks quoting two-way markets, a capital committee rationing balance sheet.
businessTypes.regulation: SEC net-capital (15c3-1), FINRA membership/exams/enforcement, SIPC. Self-regulates via FINRA (archetypal SRO), registered-principal supervision.
businessTypes.examples: Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Evercore, Jefferies

businessTypes.name: Asset Manager (Mutual Funds / ETFs / Institutional)
businessTypes.definition: Fiduciary investing pooled client capital for a fee.
businessTypes.operations: Basis-point fees on AUM; portfolio management/research, best execution, daily NAV, distribution.
businessTypes.regulation: '40 Acts (Advisers, Company), DOL ERISA. Self-regulates via ICI, CFA Institute GIPS/ethics, independent fund directors.
businessTypes.examples: BlackRock, Vanguard, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price

businessTypes.name: Private Equity / Private Credit / Venture Capital Firm
businessTypes.definition: Alternative manager raising closed-end funds to buy companies, lend directly, or fund startups.
businessTypes.operations: 2-and-20 model; value creation via leverage, operational improvement, multiple expansion; deal sourcing/diligence, portfolio board governance, LP fundraising.
businessTypes.regulation: SEC adviser registration, Form ADV/PF; HSR antitrust; leveraged-lending oversight. Self-regulates via ILPA reporting.

businessTypes.name: Life & Annuity Insurance Carrier
businessTypes.definition: Underwrites mortality/longevity risk; long-duration premium reserves invested in bonds/alternatives.
businessTypes.operations: Mortality margin, investment spread, product fees; actuarial pricing/valuation, underwriting, asset-liability matching.
businessTypes.regulation: State departments via NAIC (RBC, reserving, market conduct); Fed for designated insurers; guaranty associations. Self-regulates via SOA/AAA standards, ACLI.

businessTypes.name: Property & Casualty Insurance Carrier
businessTypes.definition: Covers property damage and liability; short-tail annual contracts repriced against loss experience.
businessTypes.operations: Underwriting profit via combined ratio plus investment income on float; pricing/underwriting risk selection, claims adjustment, catastrophe modeling, reinsurance buying.
businessTypes.regulation: State commissioners (rates/forms/solvency) via NAIC. Self-regulates via ISO/Verisk forms, CAS standards.

businessTypes.name: Reinsurer
businessTypes.definition: Insurer of insurers; assumes risk portfolios via treaty/facultative contracts.
businessTypes.operations: Underwriting margin priced with cat models plus float returns; retrocession and cat bonds lay off peak risk. Jan-1 treaty renewals.
businessTypes.regulation: Domiciliary supervisors (BMA, state, EIOPA/Solvency II); credit-for-reinsurance rules. Self-regulates via rating-agency capital discipline.
businessTypes.examples: Munich Re, Swiss Re, Berkshire Hathaway Re, RenaissanceRe

businessTypes.name: Insurance Agency & Brokerage
businessTypes.definition: Distribution intermediary placing clients' risks with carriers; earns commissions/fees without bearing underwriting risk.
businessTypes.operations: Commission (10-15% of premium) plus large-account consulting; renewal-annuity business, consolidating via roll-ups.
businessTypes.regulation: State producer licensing, fiduciary-fund and disclosure rules. Self-regulates via Big I, CIAB, E&O-driven practices.
businessTypes.examples: Marsh McLennan, Aon, Arthur J. Gallagher, HUB International

businessTypes.name: Credit Union
businessTypes.operations: Bank spread model returning margin to members; one-member-one-vote governance.
businessTypes.regulation: NCUA (federal) or state, NCUSIF share insurance; CFPB above $10B. Self-regulates via America's Credit Unions.
businessTypes.examples: Navy Federal, State Employees' CU, PenFed

businessTypes.name: Payments Network & Processor (Fintech Infrastructure)
businessTypes.definition: Operates the rails of money movement: card networks, acquirers, real-time infrastructure.
businessTypes.operations: Per-transaction economics; five-nines authorization uptime, millisecond fraud scoring, merchant onboarding, chargeback processing.
businessTypes.regulation: Money-transmitter (state), Fed (Reg II), CFPB (Reg E), FinCEN AML. Self-regulates via PCI-DSS, Nacha, EMVCo.

businessTypes.name: Digital Lender / Neobank (Fintech)
businessTypes.definition: Technology-first banking/lending/investing atop a sponsor bank's charter.
businessTypes.operations: Interchange, interest/origination fees, subscriptions; ML credit models, compliance-as-code KYC, continuous deployment.
businessTypes.regulation: Sponsor-bank supervisors, state lending/money-transmission, CFPB fair-lending/UDAAP, FTC. Self-regulates via SR 11-7-patterned model-risk governance.

businessTypes.name: Securities & Derivatives Exchange / Clearinghouse
businessTypes.definition: Regulated marketplace that lists instruments, matches buyers/sellers, publishes prices, and (via CCP clearing) guarantees settlement.
businessTypes.operations: Transaction fees, market-data licensing, listing/clearing fees; CCPs manage default risk with margin and guaranty funds (Cover-2); microsecond matching, real-time surveillance, twice-daily margin cycles.
businessTypes.regulation: SEC/CFTC market structure; SIFMU CCPs under Fed Title VIII. Exchanges are themselves SROs.

businessTypes.name: Hedge Fund / Proprietary Trading Firm
businessTypes.definition: Private vehicle pursuing absolute returns with flexible mandates and leverage; prop firms trade own capital.
businessTypes.operations: Management plus incentive fees (HF) or bid-ask/arbitrage at scale (prop/HFT); research/signal generation, risk management against drawdown limits, prime-broker financing.
businessTypes.regulation: SEC adviser registration, Form PF; CFTC/NFA; Reg SHO, 15c3-5. Self-regulates via MFA/AIMA, investor ODD.
businessTypes.examples: Citadel, Bridgewater, Jane Street, Renaissance Technologies

businessTypes.name: Mortgage Bank & Servicer
businessTypes.definition: Originates residential mortgages for sale into GSE/Ginnie securitizations and services loans.
businessTypes.operations: Gain-on-sale margins (origination) plus servicing strips (natural rate hedge); loan manufacturing to agency specs, TBA pipeline hedging, servicing call centers, loss mitigation.
businessTypes.regulation: CFPB (TRID, servicing, ATR), state NMLS, FHFA via GSE guides, HUD/FHA. Self-regulates via MBA, GSE rep-and-warrant QC.
businessTypes.examples: Rocket Mortgage, United Wholesale Mortgage, Mr. Cooper

regulators.name: Federal Reserve System
regulators.role: Supervises bank holding companies and SIFIs, sets capital/stress-testing (CCAR), operates payment systems (Fedwire, FedNow), lender of last resort.

regulators.name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.role: Regulates securities issuance/disclosure, exchanges, broker-dealers, advisers, funds; enforces antifraud; oversees SROs.

regulators.name: Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC)
regulators.role: Insures deposits to $250k, examines state nonmember banks, resolves failed banks as receiver.

regulators.name: Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC)
regulators.role: Charters/examines national banks and federal savings associations; sets safety-and-soundness and permissible-activity boundaries.

regulators.name: Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)
regulators.role: Regulates futures, options, swaps (DCMs, clearinghouses, FCMs, swap dealers); prosecutes manipulation.

regulators.name: Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA)
regulators.role: SRO for ~3,300 broker-dealers: conduct rules, licensing (SIE, Series 7), exams, surveillance, arbitration under SEC oversight.

regulators.name: NAIC / State Insurance Departments
regulators.role: License carriers/producers, approve rates/forms, conduct solvency exams; NAIC coordinates via model laws and RBC.

regulators.name: Basel Committee / Financial Stability Board
regulators.role: Basel sets bank capital/liquidity/leverage standards; FSB designates G-SIBs and coordinates crisis-prevention policy.

groundView.orgModel: Board whose risk and audit committees carry regulatory force, atop a CEO and executive committee split into revenue divisions (consumer, commercial, markets, wealth/asset management) and independent control functions: CRO's second line of defense, Compliance, Internal Audit reporting to the board. The distinctive architecture is the three lines of defense: front-office businesses own risk, independent risk/compliance constrain it, audit assures both. Compensation is heavily variable and deferred, itself a regulatory instrument for aligning risk horizons.

positions.title: Board Director / Risk Committee Chair
positions.duties: Approves risk-appetite statements, capital plans submitted to the Fed, and executive comp structures; meets examiners; owns board-level response to supervisory findings (MRAs/MRIAs).

positions.title: Chief Executive Officer
positions.duties: Allocates capital across businesses within regulatory ratios, owns the primary-supervisor relationship, sets risk culture, answers to markets quarterly.

positions.title: Chief Risk Officer
positions.duties: Runs the independent second line: sets credit, market, liquidity, operational risk limits; owns stress testing and the risk-appetite framework; can veto transactions and escalate directly to the board.

positions.title: Chief Financial Officer
positions.duties: Owns the balance sheet: capital planning (CCAR), funding/liquidity strategy, investor relations, regulatory financial reporting; runs treasury's interest-rate positioning.

positions.title: Chief Compliance Officer / BSA Officer
positions.duties: Owns adherence to the rulebook: AML/BSA program (statutory officer role), sanctions screening, fair lending, suitability, compliance testing; supervises SAR decisions.

positions.title: Head of Investment Banking / Division Head
positions.duties: Runs a revenue division's P&L; chairs commitment committees that approve underwriting exposures.

positions.title: Managing Director, M&A / Coverage Banker
positions.duties: Owns C-suite client relationships, originates mandates, quarterbacks live deals; carries a personal revenue expectation.

positions.title: Branch / Market Manager (Retail Banking)
positions.duties: Runs branches: staffing/coaching, deposit and loan growth, operational integrity (cash audits, dual control), CRA expectations.

positions.title: Portfolio Manager
positions.duties: Owns investment decisions against a benchmark: position sizing, risk budgeting, sell discipline.

positions.title: Derivatives Trader (Rates/FX/Equities Desk)
positions.duties: Makes markets and manages the desk's book: quotes prices, hedges greeks continuously, runs risk within VaR and stress limits marked to market nightly.

positions.title: Credit Analyst / Underwriter (Commercial Lending)
positions.reportsTo: Chief Credit Officer / Senior Credit Manager
positions.duties: Spreads financials, models cash-flow coverage and collateral, writes credit approval memos, assigns risk ratings, monitors covenants.

positions.title: Actuary
positions.duties: Prices products and values reserves: builds mortality/loss-development models, signs statutory reserve-adequacy opinions, tests capital under stress.

positions.title: Quantitative Analyst / Model Developer
positions.duties: Builds and validates models that price derivatives, score credit, detect fraud, compute capital; documents to SR 11-7 model-risk standards.

positions.title: Financial Advisor / Wealth Manager
positions.duties: Advises households on portfolios/retirement/estate under Reg BI or fiduciary duty; prospects and retains a book.

positions.title: Compliance Analyst / AML Investigator
positions.duties: Clears transaction-monitoring alerts, investigates suspicious activity and drafts SAR narratives, performs EDD, screens OFAC sanctions.

positions.title: Insurance Claims Adjuster
positions.duties: Investigates losses, sets reserves, negotiates settlements, detects fraud; works a pending inventory of 50-150 claims.

positions.title: Loan Officer / Mortgage Loan Originator
positions.duties: Sources borrowers, structures applications, quotes and locks rates, shepherds files to closing under TRID deadlines.

positions.title: Bank Teller / Universal Banker
positions.duties: Processes deposits/withdrawals/payments with dual-control cash handling; balances a drawer daily; flags structuring/elder-fraud to BSA.

positions.title: Trade Settlement / Operations Specialist
positions.duties: Affirms, confirms, settles trades on T+1; investigates breaks between blotters, custodians, DTCC; processes corporate actions and margin calls.

positions.title: Fraud & Disputes Specialist (Cards/Payments)
positions.duties: Works real-time fraud queues: reviews flagged transactions, blocks/reissues cards, processes Reg E/Z disputes within statutory timelines.
